newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Typhoon Winnie strikes Taiwan, kills three.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Winnie strikes Taiwan, kills three.

text.p: The first typhoon to hit Taiwan this year killed at least three people on Monday and was gaining strength, officials and news reports said.
Torrential rain swamped houses in low-lying areas of the capital, Taipei. Many roads were flooded and scores of vehicles submerged.
The rain and accelerating winds also triggered landslides, damaging houses and blocking traffic in mountainous areas, officials said.
Police said one man drowned when fishing in a river in the northeastern county of Ilan and another was killed when his house collapsed in Taipei county.
State media said Typhoon Winnie blew another man from a seven-storey building in Ilan, but police have not confirmed the report.
A 16-year-old was missing at a beach in eastern Taitung, while some 23 people were reported injured nationwide.
Winnie was 290 km (180 miles) northeast of Taipei and moving west-north-west at 21 kph (13 mph), the Central Weather Bureau said.
"North and northeastern Taiwan have entered Typhoon Winnie's range and the typhoon's speed is increasing," the Central Weather Bureau said.
The bureau also said the wind and rain would intensify later in the day.
The typhoon, packing maximum sustained winds of 144 km per hour (89 miles per hour) and gusts of up to 180 kph (112 mph), forced government agencies, financial markets and schools to close.
All domestic flights were cancelled but international flights were running to schedule.
